summary: William Hoyles Drew (1805–1856) was an Indology scholar who studied under traditional teacher Ramanujan. He served with the London Missionary Society as chaplain of the Madras Chapel from 1834 to 1856.

William Hunter (1755–1812) worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned an M.A. from the University of Aberdeen (~1773–1777). He served in the East India Company, as surgeon at Agra Residency (~1794–1806), and at Fort William College (1805–1811).

William Irvine (1840–1911) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at King's College London (~1860–1862) and served as a civil servant in the Indian Civil Service from 1864 to 1888.

William J. Gedney (1915–1999) was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. under Franklin Edgerton at Yale University (~1941–1947). He later served as Professor of Linguistics at the University of Ceylon (1959–1960) and the University of Michigan (1960–1981).

William James (1842–1910) worked in philosophy and religious studies. Educated at Harvard, including a medical degree (1864–1869), he had a long career at Harvard University as a lecturer in physiology (1872), assistant professor, and professor from 1885.

William Jones (1746–1794) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at University College, Oxford. In 1783, he became Chief Justice at Fort William and a judge of the Calcutta High Court, and he founded The Asiatic Society in 1784.

William Joseph Wilkins (1843–1902) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Hackney College (~1863–1868) and served as a teacher with the London Missionary Society and the Bhowanipore Missionary Institution from ~1868 to 1884.

William Knighton (1824–1900) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as headmaster at Norman Seminary, Colombo (~1845–1847), Lecturer in History and Logic at Presidency University (1846), and held a post in the Indian Civil Service.

William L. Ames is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Washington under Collett Cox and David Seyfort Ruegg, and held posts at the University of Washington and John F. Kennedy University.

William Lee-Warner (1846–1914) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After earning a B.A. from St John's College (1865–1869), he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1869–1895) and was a Fellow of the University of Mumbai.

William Linwood (1817–1878) worked in Indology and linguistics. Educated at Christ Church, Oxford, where he earned a B.A. and M.A. (~1836–1842), he later taught at Shrewsbury School and served as a public examiner at Oxford in 1850.

William Logan (1841–1914) was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology who studied at the University of Edinburgh. He served in the Madras Civil Service (1862–1888) and became a Fellow of the University of Madras in 1882.

William M. Bodiford (b. 1955) specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. After earning his Ph.D. at Yale under Stanley Weinstein, he held positions at Davidson College and the University of Iowa before a long career at UCLA.

William M. Gorvine is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Virginia in 2006 under David Germano and held a post at the University of Virginia (attested 1995).
William MacColin Kirkpatrick (1878–1953) was an Indology scholar who studied at Bishop Cotton School and served in the Indian Civil Service.

William Markby (1829–1914) worked in Indology and other fields, earning a DCL at Oxford. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta (~1877–1878) and Reader in Indian Law at Oxford (1878–1900).

William McCulloch (1856–1928) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Edinburgh, among other institutions. In 1886, he served as Principal of Chinsurah Theological College.

William McGrath is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his MA-PhD at the University of Virginia (2010–2017). He was appointed Assistant Professor at New York University in 2021.

William Montgomery McGovern (1897–1964) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. After completing a D.Phil. at Christ Church, Oxford, he lectured at SOAS (1918–1924) and became Professor of Far Eastern Studies at Northwestern University in 1929.

William Nassau Lees (1825–1889) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and history. Educated at Trinity College Dublin, he served as Secretary to the Board of Examiners at Fort William (~1853–1869) and Principal and Professor at Aliah University (~1856–1870).
